_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 5 Mathematics unit lecture film, Squares, Cubes and Roots. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. The three chapters squares/sqroots and cubes/cuberoots split the WORK dict's first two parts (Squares and roots; Cubes and cube roots) into a build chapter and a roots chapter each, because a root is a distinct idea (the inverse question) from the number itself; triangular carries the third part whole. Every number said is the lesson's own: 4x4=16 and the first five squares (squares-cubes-and-roots.html Step 1), the L-shape of 3+3+1=7 turning 3x3 into 4x4 and the odd-number sum 1+3+5+7=16 (Step 2), 50 sitting one dot short of the next square with 49 the biggest square below it - Step 3's own selectable numbers (NUMS3) and its own default (num3 = 50), not the 15/9/6 an earlier draft invented, which Step 3 cannot even select - and the squares to 12 squared (Step 3's note), 7 squared/49 and its root (Step 4), 3 cubed/27 with the two common wrong answers 9 (Step 5), the two roots of 64 and the six cube numbers 1/8/27/64/125/216 against fourteen squares up to 216 (Step 6), the triangular totals 1/3/6/10 and the 4-by-5-rectangle trick (Step 7), and the neighbouring-triangulars-make-a-square fact 6+10=16 from Step 7's own note.
title: Squares, Cubes and Roots
subtitle: Grade 5 Mathematics
objectives: Use knowledge of multiplication to recognise square numbers (from 1 to 100).
Recognise and extend the spatial pattern of square and triangular numbers.
Use knowledge of multiplication and square numbers to recognise cube numbers (from 1 to 125).

beats.say: Multiply a number by itself, and you get a square number.
Do it again, and you get a cube, or a triangle of dots.
Four rows of four dots make a square: four squared.
Four squared means four times four, which is sixteen.
The first square numbers are one, four, nine, sixteen, twenty five.

at.list: one, four, nine, sixteen, twenty five

beats.say: Turn a three by three square into a four by four one.
That adds an L shape of seven new dots: three, three, and one.
Odd numbers build squares: one, plus three, plus five, plus seven.
Not every number is a square number.
The biggest square under fifty is forty nine, so one dot is left over.
Know squares to twelve squared: one, four, nine, to a hundred forty four.
Seven squared is forty nine. What is the square root of forty nine?

at.root: the square root of forty nine

beats.say: The square root of forty nine is seven: squaring undoes rooting.

at.rootans: The square root of forty nine is seven

beats.say: A cube number multiplies a number by itself three times.
Three cubed is three times three times three, which is twenty seven.
It is not three plus three plus three, and not three times three.
A cube is a square, stacked three layers high.
Each layer is a three by three square of nine blocks.
A cube root asks the opposite: how many blocks on each edge?

at.edge: how many blocks on each edge

beats.say: Sixty four is four times four times four; its cube root is four.

at.sixtyfour: Sixty four is four times four times four

beats.say: But the square root of sixty four is eight: eight times eight.

at.sqrt64: the square root of sixty four is eight

beats.say: The six cube numbers to know are one, eight, twenty seven and sixty four.

at.sixcubes: The six cube numbers to know
at.listA: one, eight, twenty seven and sixty four

beats.say: Then one hundred twenty five, and two hundred sixteen.
Up to two hundred sixteen, there are fourteen squares but only six cubes.

at.fourteen6: fourteen squares but only six cubes

beats.say: A triangular number is built from rows that grow by one.
One row, then two, then three: the totals are one, three, six.

at.rows123: One row, then two, then three

beats.say: Four rows make ten dots, drawn as a triangle.
A second triangle, upside down, turns it into a rectangle.
Four rows by five columns is twenty, so one triangle is ten.
Six plus ten is sixteen: two triangular numbers make a square.

at.squarefact: two triangular numbers make a square

beats.say: A square number is a number times itself: four squared is sixteen.
A cube number multiplies it three times: three cubed is twenty seven.
Roots undo them: the square root of forty nine is seven.

at.root2: the square root of forty nine is seven

beats.say: And triangular numbers grow from rows: one, three, six, ten.
